title: I built a ghibli style train sim world using Astra
author: aniketjatav
selftext:
Recently built this ghibli style train journey sim game. Where you navigate through floating towns and deliver passengers.

Entire build was done using Astra, cooked about half my weekly usage lol. Also used a 2.5d workflows, characters and some parts are 2d whereas the world is entirely 3d.

Game demo: Play here

replies.author: Rasrey
replies.body: You are using the same model with insufficiently specific prompts. Out-of-the-box Astra, if you will. comments.author: pickleunicorn
comments.body:
I really like the overall vibe! But there are still many issues at the moment, and one that is making me want to stop playing : the lantern thing that makes my train stop abruptly and even makes me go back to the train station. I want to keep riding and I don't want to run the same road that I just ran. So, aside the fact that some sprites need to be reworked a bit, that the game needs a bit of optimization in some areas, and that the big animals are completely buggy, the things I think that would be really good to the game are : 

\- push the game to be a scory one, the better you drive, the best score you have; and you can add more mechanics to improve that score throughout the run

\- do not stop the train; we want to ride so please do not stop it

\- remove mechanics that needs us to slow down (like John Doe wants to look at the view)

\- improve the speed control because the top speed is slow and if we hold off the W key the train slows down very quickly, so currently we don't want to slow down at all; if we can go to higher speed and the speed control is better, then it will make us want to drive better; for example if we go to top speed in a turn we can just fall off from the track, it would be fun and we would really want to improve our driving

\- having the people screaming louder and louder if the balance is wrong and if we fall would be really immersive and enjoyable

\- a MUST would be to have a generated world on each run, it would improve the replayability very much
